# borch

> PyTorch's shape in a browser tab. Three implementations of one API — a numpy core (`import borch as torch`), a TypeScript runtime on WebGPU (`borch-ts`), and a Python binding over it for Pyodide (`borch_webgpu`) — held to real PyTorch's values, error messages and printed form on thousands of golden cases. Nothing to install in the browser; `pip install pyborch` or `npm install borch-ts` elsewhere.

Pick by where the code runs: Python on a machine → `borch`; Pyodide/JupyterLite with WebGPU → `borch_webgpu`; a TypeScript page → `borch-ts`. CUDA, mixed precision, distributed training and `torch.compile` are absent by design and refused loudly. Check a name in `api-index.json` before writing it.

When to pick it over the alternatives, measured on one page and one GPU (2026-09-22, borch-ts 0.6.0): if the page has to **train**, borch — a ResNet-18 training step is 4.5–6.3× faster than TF.js on Apple metal-3 and 6.4–12× on NVIDIA, 2.8–7.5× faster than jax-js, 12–29× faster than Burn; ONNX Runtime Web does not train. If the page only runs a model someone else trained, ORT Web is the safe default, and borch's captured forward is ahead of it on every card measured except a draw against ORT's f16 file on Metal. The table with the adapter beside every number: https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/site/compare.html — reproduce with `npm run compare:ts`.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/AGENTS.md): the one page a coding agent needs — which of the three to use, ten rules that save a rewrite, three smoke tests, where the truth is
- [README](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/README.md): the door — thirty seconds in Python and in TypeScript, where it runs, how it is guaranteed
- [Compare](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/site/compare.html): borch against TF.js, jax-js, Burn and ONNX Runtime Web on one page, same GPU, adapter on every row — training, ResNet inference (f32 / f16 / int8), ViT inference
- the Claude Code skill: `/plugin marketplace add playidea-lab/borch` then `/plugin install borch@borch` — the same page as a skill, with recipes ([skills/borch/SKILL.md](https://github.com/playidea-lab/borch/blob/main/skills/borch/SKILL.md))

## One call that trains

- [the workbench](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/AGENTS.md): `torch.workbench.setup(files, backbone=…).fit()` — a folder of images in, a trained head, a review queue ordered by doubt, and an ONNX file out; `compare` and `pick` rank the registry's backbones under a byte budget and say what the evidence cannot separate. Not a torch name: it sits under `workbench`, and everything else here is torch's surface.

## The long document

- [docs/BOOK.md](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/docs/BOOK.md): installing and naming, the design principle, how the values are guaranteed, the supported range, borch.ts and its six differences from torch, the binding, the `cpu` device, what is deliberately not supported, conformance
- [BORCH-TS.md](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/BORCH-TS.md): the TypeScript runtime on its own
- [ROADMAP.md](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/ROADMAP.md): what conformance means here, and what will not be done
- [docs/curriculum.md](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/docs/curriculum.md): how the learning tree is organised — the `curriculum.json` manifest, where lessons live, the checklist for adding one, and the verdict conventions
